findings.passage: When you arrive at your polling place to vote, state law requires you to either show a picture ID or sign an affidavit attesting that you are not in possession of a picture ID.
findings.note: From an elections guide posted on his Senate page and written in his name. It describes the in-person rule as it stood in 2022: show picture ID or sign an affidavit. The same page adds that a voter with no picture ID can vote like any other voter by signing an affidavit provided at the polls. It describes the law and does not say whether he wants it changed.
subjects: voter with no ID: sworn affidavit

findings.passage: This is the flexibility and consideration our servicemembers have been asking for, and this is a direct execution of the will of the Michigan people this past November.
findings.note: Quote in his Senate press release about SB 259 (absentee ballots of military voters counted if received up to six days after the election), which the release calls the first bill implementing the 2022 ballot measure. The release lists that measure's photo-ID-or-affidavit rule for in-person voting and for applying for an absentee ballot; that list is the release's text, not a quote of him.
subjects: voter ID or affidavit under the 2022 ballot measure
